newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on weak peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on weak peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 75 basis points at 18.75 percent on Tuesday to offset early peso weakness, traders said.
"The peso was very soft and that is why we saw upside pressure on overnight rates, to ease pressure on the peso," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts weakened 2.5 centavos to 8.0020/8.0050 per dollar in early trade, but reversed losses to end 3.7 centavos firmer at 7.9380/7.9430 per dollar.
Dealers said higher secondary rates attracted foreign capital which helped bolster the peso.
"U.S. long bond yields dived and then we began to see foreigners step in, and that made the peso recover," another trader said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 1-17/32 in late trade to yield 6.98 percent.

Dealers said overnight rates reached a session low of 18.00 percent on a wave of buying triggered when the central bank drained a lot less liquidity through selling paper than on many recent sessions.

"Banco de Mexico didn't inject any paper into the secondary market today. It had previously been selling and selling and the glut of paper in recent days prevented rates from falling any further," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico drained just 204 million pesos from the market through one single overnight repo which it assigned at 18.20 percent.
"When the central bank completed its participation, buyers stepped in and rates dropped," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended up 35 basis points at 19.00 percent.
June contracts on the Cetes futures market in Chicago ended up 34 centavos at 77.74 pesos.

Liquidity of 6.342 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation. Traders said the resulting liquidity surplus would increase due to an overplacement of 1.800 billion pesos from the primary auction.
Nonetheless, liquidity was expected to flow out of the system due to month-end demand for cash and 7.500 billion pesos in tax payments falling due.
